date: 11-329 H (632-941); formation of the schools 1st-4th century H.
title: 1pv0fas
The emergence of the sects and schools
hook: How did a single Ummah travel from political divisions to circles of learning and schools of jurisprudence?
scenes.0.text: In the reports, the "Shi'at Ali," the partisans of Imam Ali, already existed in the Prophet's time. This attachment came about through the Prophet's guidance. Those who hold this view link it with Ghadir Khumm and similar events. TDV writes that the word "Shia" means "partisan." As a term, it describes the groups that maintain that leadership after the Prophet belongs to Imam Ali and his descendants.

scenes.1.text: For Bayyina 98:7, a report is transmitted in which the Prophet says to Imam Ali, "This is you and your Shia." Those who hold this view regard it as evidence that the word "Shia" was used in the Prophet's time. The authenticity of the report is disputed among hadith scholars. Its relation to the verse and its chains of transmission must be checked separately in the books.

scenes.2.text: After the Prophet's death, Abu Bakr was chosen at Saqifa, and Imam Ali's bay'a was delayed. TDV mentions Salman al-Farisi, Abu Dharr, Miqdad and Ammar among the partisans of Imam Ali and writes that this attachment arose from a political choice. In the reports, the same Companions are mentioned as those who remained faithful to the Prophet's bequest concerning the imamate.

scenes.3.text: The Camel and Siffin split the Ummah's political unity. At Siffin, Mu'awiya's army fixed pages of the Quran on spears and asked for arbitration. A group from Imam Ali's army accepted the arbitration despite his objection. Then, saying "judgment belongs only to God," they separated and withdrew to Harura. These are the first Kharijites, the Muhakkima. Imam Ali fought them at Nahrawan (658). The Kharijites considered one who commits a major sin an unbeliever. In response to this, the Murji'a arose, who leave the fate of persons to God (about 680-694). Those who remained attached to Imam Ali formed the Shia. These events

scenes.4.text: The martyrdom of Imam Husayn at Karbala deeply affected the Shia. In Kufa, al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi rose up in 66 H. (685) to call the martyrs' killers to account, and ruled Kufa for about 18 months. He was killed in 67. The report that he made his call in the name of Muhammad b. al-Hanafiyya is tied to the birth of the Kaysaniyya. The reports differ in their view of al-Mukhtar. Most mention him favorably. Some scholars, such as Majlisi, prefer to remain silent. Whether the Kaysaniyya emerged from al-Mukhtar or after his death is also disputed.
scenes.4.art.actors.0.label: 16t2eyg
Al-Mukhtar al-Thaqafi
scenes.5.text: Zayd b. Ali, a grandson of Imam Husayn, rose up in Kufa in 122 H. (740) against the Umayyad caliph Hisham and was killed. Zayd gave the imamate to the most virtuous of the descendants of Imam Ali who rises up. He also regarded the caliphates of Caliph Abu Bakr and Caliph Umar as legitimate. This line became a separate branch under the name Zaydiyya. It founded states in Tabaristan and Yemen. TDV describes it as a moderate Shia sect. In Imami Shia sources, however, the imamate is described by nass, that is, by explicit designation.
scenes.5.art.actors.0.label: 19100mv
Zayd b. Ali
scenes.6.text: While Umayyad rule was weakening and Abbasid rule had not yet settled, Imam Muhammad al-Baqir and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq established a wide circle of learning in Medina. About 3200 narrators transmit from him in Shaykh al-Tusi's Rijal, and about 4000 according to al-Mufid. Ja'fari jurisprudence consists largely of his reports. The compilations called the Four Hundred Usul are attributed to his students. It occurs in the reports that Malik took hadith from him and that Abu Hanifa regarded him as the most learned person of his age. In the Sunni account, this relationship is mentioned as an exchange of hadith and scholarly respect.
scenes.6.art.actors.0.label: 1ytn1vq
Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq
scenes.7.text: In the same centuries the Sunni schools of jurisprudence and theology also took shape: Abu Hanifa (d. 150), Malik (d. 179), al-Shafi'i (d. 204) and Ahmad b. Hanbal (d. 241). The term "Ahl al-Sunna," according to TDV, became established in the 3rd/9th century. In theology, the schools of al-Ash'ari (d. 324) and al-Maturidi (d. 333) arose. There are some theological affinities between the Mu'tazila, which gives wide place to reason, and the Shia. TDV writes that the Zaydiyya is close to the Mu'tazila. The basic divergence of the schools is over the imamate, the caliphate and the sources of hadith.

scenes.8.text: When Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's eldest son Isma'il died before his father, or was thought to have died, a split arose over the imamate. Those who continued Isma'il's imamate founded the Isma'iliyya and went on with his son Muhammad b. Isma'il. The later Fatimid state (909-1171) came from this branch. The majority, however, attached themselves to Imam Musa al-Kazim. This branch is the Twelver Shia. Imam Musa al-Kazim was arrested in Baghdad under pressure from Harun al-Rashid and died in 183 (799). The occultation of the Twelfth Imam began in 260, according to the reports. The minor occultation lasts 260-329, followed by the major occultation. Thus the Twelver Shia was completed.

sunni.0.says: The term's becoming established in the 3rd/9th century; the schools of al-Ash'ari (d. 324) and al-Maturidi (d. 333); the Hanbali-Salafi hadith line; Abu Hanifa, Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad b. Hanbal.
sunni.1.says: The Siffin arbitration, the Muhakkima withdrawing to Harura, Nahrawan (658).
sunni.2.says: The emergence of the Murji'a against the Kharijites' takfir (about 680-694), the understanding of faith, relation with Abu Hanifa.
sunni.3.says: The report that Imam Ali and his Shia are "khayr al-bariyya."

disputes.0.title: 7kdzd7
When was the Shia born?
disputes.0.shia: Attachment to Imam Ali reaches back to the Companions' era in both accounts. In Shia sources, the Shi'at Ali existed in the Prophet's time, and the Bayyina 98:7 report is regarded as evidence for this.
disputes.0.sunni: Attachment to Imam Ali reaches back to the Companions' era in both accounts. In the Sunni account, the term became established after Saqifa as a political partisanship; the authenticity of the Bayyina report is disputed.
disputes.1.title: t0pwle
Imamate: nass or election?
disputes.1.shia: The caliphate and the imamate are the question to which both traditions seek an answer. In Shia belief, this office was given by nass to Imam Ali and the twelve imams from his descendants; the Zaydiyya, however, regards the most virtuous child of Imam Ali who rises up as the imam.
disputes.1.sunni: The caliphate and the imamate are the question to which both traditions seek an answer. In the Ahl al-Sunna, the caliph is determined at Saqifa and afterward by shura and bay'a, and this is grounded in the Companions' choice.
disputes.2.title: 1dy3h6r
The relation of the Ja'fari school to the Sunni schools
disputes.2.shia: Malik's and Abu Hanifa's scholarly relationship with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq is mentioned in both sources. In the Shia account, both benefited from his teaching circle; Ja'fari jurisprudence rests on the imams' reports.
disputes.2.sunni: Malik's and Abu Hanifa's scholarly relationship with Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq is mentioned in both sources. In the Sunni account, Malik's taking hadith and his respect are accepted; the report of discipleship rests on secondary sources, and Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq is considered trustworthy in hadith.
disputes.3.title: 11h73t5
Why did Isma'il not become imam?
disputes.3.shia: Isma'il's dying before his father is the commonly narrated beginning of the split. The Imami Shia accept that Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq chose Imam Musa al-Kazim.
disputes.3.sunni: Isma'il's dying before his father is the commonly narrated beginning of the split. Sunni sources relate this as a split within the Shia; TDV gives his death, his being seen alive and the claim of wine-drinking as separate reports.
questions.0: Partisanship of Imam Ali is described both for the Prophet's time and for after Saqifa. To understand the history of a concept, which sources need to be read side by side?
questions.1: The Kharijites answered the major sin with takfir, while the Murji'a answered by leaving the outcome to God. How do two different answers to the same crisis affect the balance of a community?
questions.2: Zayd b. Ali chose uprising, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq chose the circle of learning. How do these two paths within the Ahl al-Bayt differ in aim and method?
questions.3: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's teaching circle is a gate mentioned by both Shia and Sunni scholars. How can a shared scholarly heritage soften later sectarian boundaries?
questions.4: The sects and schools began with political divisions and turned into schools of jurisprudence and theology. On this journey, how did learning help keep the community together?
summary: The Ummah's paths diverged through Saqifa, the Camel, Siffin and Karbala. Around the Ahl al-Bayt, the Zaydiyya, the Isma'iliyya and the Twelver Shia formed. In the other circle, the four schools of jurisprudence and the Ash'ari and Maturidi schools of theology arose.
key: The birth of the schools from Saqifa to Karbala
notes.0: The sects and schools first arose from political divisions (Saqifa, the Camel, Siffin, Karbala).
notes.1: After Karbala, al-Mukhtar's revolt and the Kaysaniyya appeared.
notes.2: The Zaydiyya was born from Zayd b. Ali's revolt.
notes.3: Isma'il's imamate led to a split; the majority attached themselves to Imam Musa al-Kazim and became the Twelver Shia.
notes.4: The Sunni schools of jurisprudence and theology took shape in the same centuries.
